Mercantilism

/MUR-kuhn-tih-liz-uhm/ - the stress falls on MUR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Mercantilism means an economic doctrine of maximizing exports and hoarding precious metals.

The colony's tobacco could sail only to home ports — mercantilism written into every bill of lading.

Worked Example

The strategy game's veterans all play the same opening. Sell your kingdom's wool to every neighbor, buy nothing back, slap harbor taxes on any rival's ship, and watch your treasury tokens stack while everyone else's dwindle. New players call it hoarding; the rulebook's designers, who studied their history, named the strategy card for what it is.

Mercantilism is the exact word on that card, because mercantilism means an economic doctrine of maximizing exports and hoarding precious metals — trade as a contest the state must win, with gold as the score. It is not simple stinginess: the mercantilist kingdom trades constantly and eagerly, but only ever in one direction, out.

How Mercantilism Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

economic nationalism

economic nationalism: trade bent to national power — the modern textbook cousin

gold-hoarding

gold-hoarding: the blunt nickname for the doctrine's scorekeeping

Antonyms

free trade

free trade: goods crossing borders untaxed, in both directions

open markets

open markets: commerce steered by buyers and sellers, not the crown

How Strong Is It? — thrift → mercantilism → autarky

thrift vs. mercantilism

thrift vs. mercantilism: Thrift is the household version — spend less than comes in, and tuck away the difference.

autarky vs. mercantilism

autarky vs. mercantilism: Autarky goes further than mercantilism — the mercantilist nation still trades busily so long as gold flows in; the autarkic one bolts the door on trade altogether.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — mercantil

Root — mercantil: of merchants and trading (Latin mercari, to trade; merx, goods)

Suffix — -ism

Suffix — -ism: system, doctrine

Put it together

Put it together: Mercantil- (of merchants and trading) + -ism = the merchants' system raised to state doctrine. Latin merx meant goods for sale, and mercari to trade them; mercantilism is what happens when a whole crown starts thinking like a merchant with one rule — always sell for more than you buy — and counts its gold to keep score.

Use the root in a new word: merchandise

Use the root in a new word: merchandise: A shop's merchandise is its goods for trade — the same merc- that once loaded the treasure fleets.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / historical

Mercantilism belongs to history essays and economics classes, and it names a complete doctrine: exports forced up, imports squeezed, bullion banked as the measure of national strength. Tariffs alone are just protection; mercantilism adds the one-way flow of gold. Its unit-mates mark the other corners — laissez-faire sends the state home, corporatism seats industries inside it, consumerism keeps the households buying.
